Official docs establish a native CRUD webservice that gives third-party tools access to shop data, with documented carts and other commerce resources. They do not establish a decoupled shopper storefront architecture or complete cart/checkout/order workflow independent of the native front office. An integration/data API alone is insufficient for the headless core; custom integration remains possible and unassessed.

Official current developer docs explicitly describe the native webservice as REST over HTTP using XML/JSON and document creation, reads and updates at the shop API endpoint. This supports the API detail independently of the unresolved storefront architecture.

The frontend README linked by mall explicitly identifies frontend/backend separation, states all storefront interfaces reside in mall-portal, and permits a separately running client to select a local or online API base URL. Its product, cart, order and payment pages consume those backend APIs. This establishes decoupled commerce architecture for the routed mall backend through functional evidence rather than a literal headless headline; no API addon is installed into mall.
